You are urban_comet97, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
10 agents form one group, and you work with brisk_harbor75, early_island22, gentle_otter27, jolly_ember22, pale_kettle84, pale_lantern48, rapid_thistle87, sandy_walnut42, zesty_lantern63. Each agent works in its own sandbox, on its
own git repository. Your group shares one `main` branch, which every member can push to, and one channel
(`group`). Work together with your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to
coordinate and share helpful findings.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is your group's final score: the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on `main` at
the end. Every agent receives the same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents announce what they are exploring, building, or have found,
and ask each other questions. Typical posts include a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a finding (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), a proposal for how to organize the work, or a question.
- `post` publishes a message to `group`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, and any unopened posts that mention you, one line each
  (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a post's number shows its full text, with its
  pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished, with a pointer, then go back
  to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main` does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve as
  many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

Modern, customizable, feature-rich and extensible `ls` replacement.
Documentation · Features · Installation · Display Formats · Command Reference

## Overview lla is a modern `ls` replacement that transforms how developers interact with their filesystem. Built with Rust's performance capabilities and designed with user experience in mind, lla combines the familiarity of `ls` with powerful features like specialized views, Git integration, and a robust plugin system with an extensible list of plugins to add more functionality. ## Features - Multiple Views: Default clean view, long format, tree structure, table layout, grid display - Diff Command: Human-friendly directory or file comparisons (local ↔ local or git) with size/line deltas and unified diff output - Git Integration: Built-in status visualization and repository insights - Advanced Organization: Timeline view, storage analysis, recursive exploration - Smart Navigation: Interactive directory jumper with bookmarks and history - Smart Search: complex filtering patterns (OR, AND, NOT, XOR), regex support, content search - Customization: Plugin system, theme manager, custom shortcuts, configurable display - High Performance: Built with Rust, modern UI, clean listings - Smart Sorting: Multiple criteria, directory-first option, natural sorting - Flexible Config: Easy initialization, plugin management, configuration tools - Rich Plugin Ecosystem: File ops and metadata enhancements, code analysis, git tools, and more - Smart Filters: Range-based size/time filters, reusable presets, cache-aware refinements - Git-aware Filtering: Optional `.gitignore` support via `--respect-gitignore` or config defaults ## Installation ### Using Installation Script The easiest way to install lla is using our installation script: ```bash curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chaqchase/lla/main/install.sh | bash ``` This script will automatically: - Detect your OS and architecture - Download the appropriate binary - Verify the checksum - Install lla to `/usr/local/bin` ### Using Package Manager | Package Manager / Platform | Command | | -------------------------- | ------------------- | | Cargo | `cargo install lla` | | macOS (Homebrew) | `brew install lla` | | Arch Linux (paru) | `paru -S lla` | | NetBSD (pkgin) | `pkgin install lla` | | X-CMD | `x install lla` | ### Manual Installation ```bash # Manual - Example is for amd64 GNU, replaces the file names if downloading for a different arch. wget -c https://github.com/chaqchase/lla/releases/download//-> -O lla # Example /v0.3.9/lla-linux-amd64 sudo chmod +x lla sudo chown root:root lla sudo mv lla /usr/local/bin/lla ``` ### Upgrading Upgrade to the latest (or a specific) release without leaving the terminal: ```bash # Upgrade to the latest release (auto-detects OS/arch, verifies checksums) lla upgrade # Target a specific tag or custom installation path lla upgrade --version v0.5.1 --path /usr/local/bin/lla ``` The upgrade command reuses the official install script logic, renders animated progress indicators, verifies the `SHA256SUMS` manifest, and atomically swaps the `lla` binary in place (defaults to the path of the running executable—override with `--path` if needed). ### Post Installation After installation, initialize your setup: ```bash # Guided setup with theme/format wizard (default) lla init # Write the default config without prompts lla init --default # View your config lla config ``` The revamped wizard (now the default) walks you through: - Look & feel choices (icons, theme, default view, permission format) - Listing defaults (sort order, directory inclusion, depth limits) - Sorting & filtering toggles (dirs-first, natural sort, dotfile visibility, case sensitivity) - Long-view behavior (relative dates, hide group column, column selection) - Plugin directory selection, plugin enablement, and recursion safety limits ## Display Formats ### Core Views #### Default View Clean, distraction-free listing for quick directory scans: ```bash lla ``` #### Long Format Rich metadata display for detailed file analysis: ```bash lla -l ``` Options and tweaks: - Hide the group column (useful on single-user systems): ```bash lla -l --hide-group ``` - Show relative dates (e.g., "2h ago"): ```bash lla -l --relative-dates ``` To make these defaults, add to your config (`~/.config/lla/config.toml`): ```toml [formatters.long] hide_group = true relative_dates = true columns = ["permissions", "size", "modified", "user", "group", "name", "field:git_status", "field:tags"] ``` The `columns` array lets you control the precise column order. Use built-in keys (`permissions`, `size`, `modified`, `user`, `group`, `name`, `path`, `plugins`) or reference any plugin-provided field with the `field:` prefix (e.g., `field:git_status`, `field:complexity_score`). #### Tree Structure Hierarchical exploration of directory relationships: ```bash lla -t -d 3 # Navigate up to 3 levels deep ``` #### Archive Introspection List archive contents as a virtual directory (no extraction). Supported: `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`. ``` lla my_archive.zip -t # tree view lla project.tar.gz -l # long view lla my_archive.tgz --json lla my_archive.zip -l -f ".rs" # filter by extension on internal paths ``` #### Single-file Listing You can pass a single file path to list it directly with any view or machine output: ``` lla README.md # default view lla Cargo.toml -l # long view lla src/main.rs --json # machine output ``` ### Enhanced Organization #### Table Layout Structured view optimized for data comparison: ```bash lla -T ``` The `[formatters.table].columns` setting mirrors the long-view syntax, so you can mix built-in fields with plugin-provided metadata: ```toml [formatters.table] columns = ["permissions", "size", "modified", "name", "field:git_branch", "field:git_commit"] ``` #### Diff View (Files & Directories) Compare directories or individual files (including against git references) with compact, colorized summaries. Directory comparisons still show the status table with size deltas, while file comparisons add a unified diff plus size/line-change stats: ```bash lla diff src ../backup/src

lla diff src ../backup/src lla diff apps/api --git # compare working tree vs HEAD lla diff src --git --git-ref HEAD~1 # compare against another commit lla diff Cargo.lock ../backup/Cargo.lock lla diff Cargo.lock --git --git-ref HEAD~1 ``` For directories, the diff view groups entries by status, colors the change indicator, and shows left/right sizes plus the net delta so you can spot growth at a glance. For files, lla prints a size summary, line-count delta, and a git-style unified diff (with automatic binary detection so unreadable data isn’t dumped to your terminal). #### Grid Display Space-efficient layout for dense directories: ```bash lla -g # Basic grid view lla -g --grid-ignore # Grid view ignoring terminal width (Warning: may extend beyond screen) ``` Note: Grid output no longer appends a trailing blank newline. ### Specialized Views #### Git Integration Smart repository insights: ```bash lla -G ``` #### Timeline Organization Chronological file tracking: ```bash lla --timeline ``` #### Storage Analysis Visual disk usage insights, including a total size summary: ```bash lla -S # use --include-dirs to calculate directory sizes (recursive; slower on large trees) ``` ### Advanced Navigation #### Jump-to-Directory (Interactive Directory Jumper) Quickly navigate to bookmarked or recently visited directories with an interactive keyboard-driven prompt: ```bash # One-time setup for seamless directory jumping lla jump --setup # Interactive directory selection lla jump # Add directory to bookmarks lla jump --add ~/projects/my-app # Remove bookmark lla jump --remove ~/projects/my-app # List all bookmarks and recent history lla jump --list # Clear history lla jump --clear-history ``` **Features:** - **Interactive Selection**: Arrow keys and Enter to select from bookmarked and recent directories - **Smart History**: Automatically records directory visits (respects `exclude_paths`) - **Bookmarks**: Add favorite directories for quick access - **Deduplication**: No duplicate entries in history - **Shell Integration**: Works seamlessly with shell commands like `cd` **How it works:** 1. Bookmarks (marked with ★) appear first in the selection list 2. Recent directories follow, showing directory name and full path 3. Use arrow keys to navigate, Enter to select 4. The selected path is printed to stdout for shell integration 5. History is automatically maintained as you navigate directories **Shell Integration Setup:** Since `lla` runs as a child process, it cannot directly change your shell's working directory. To enable seamless directory jumping, run the automatic setup: ```bash lla jump --setup ``` This will automatically detect your shell (bash, zsh, or fish) and add the necessary function to your shell configuration file. After setup, restart your terminal or run `source ~/.zshrc` (or equivalent for your shell). Then use `j` to jump to directories interactively! **Examples:** ```bash # One-time setup (auto-detects your shell) lla jump --setup # shell override lla jump --setup --shell fish # Navigate to a frequently used directory (after setup) j # Add your project directories to bookmarks lla jump --add ~/dev/my-project lla jump --add ~/work/client-app lla jump --add ~/personal/blog # View all your saved locations lla jump --list ``` #### Fuzzy Search (Experimental) Interactive file discovery with multi-select and batch actions: ```bash lla --fuzzy ``` Keyboard shortcuts: - Ctrl+J / Ctrl+K: move down / up - Ctrl+N / Ctrl+P: move down / up - Ctrl+D / Ctrl+U: half-page down / up - Ctrl+G: jump to end - Ctrl+Shift+G: jump to start - Ctrl+C / Esc: exit - Space: toggle select - Enter: confirm (returns the highlighted file or all selected files) - Ctrl+E: open selected file(s) in your editor - Ctrl+Y: copy selected path(s) to clipboard - Ctrl+O: open selected file(s) with the system opener (open/xdg-open/start) - F2: rename the highlighted file (Enter: confirm, Esc/Ctrl+C: cancel) Search input shortcuts: - Ctrl+W: delete word backward - Ctrl+H: delete character (backspace) - Ctrl+A: jump to start of input (`Home` also works) - End: jump to end of input Editor selection (for `Ctrl+E`): - Config override: `listers.fuzzy.editor` (takes priority) - Environment: `$EDITOR`, then `$VISUAL` - Fallback: `nano` (macOS/Linux) or `notepad` (Windows) Example config: ```toml [listers.fuzzy] editor = "nvim" # or: "code --wait" ``` Tip: for GUI editors, configure a “wait” flag so lla returns after you close the file, e.g. `code --wait` or `subl -w`. #### Deep Directory Exploration (Recursive) Comprehensive subdirectory listing: ```bash lla -R lla -R -d 3 # Set exploration depth ``` The `-R` option can be integrated with other options to create a more specific view. For example, `lla -R -l` will show a detailed listing of all files and directories in the current directory. ### Content Search Powerful ripgrep-backed content search with syntax highlighting and theme integration: ```bash lla --search "TODO" ``` **Features:** - **Syntax Highlighting**: Code snippets are automatically highlighted based on file extension - **Match Indicators**: Bright yellow carets (^^^) point to exact match locations - **Context Control**: Configurable context lines around matches (`--search-context`) - **Theme Integration**: Colors adapt to your current lla theme - **Safe by Default**: Uses literal string matching; add `regex:` prefix for regex patterns - **Filter Integration**: Honors all existing filters, exclude paths, and dotfile settings **Examples:** ```bash # Basic content search lla --search "main()" # Search with more context lla --search "TODO" --search-context 5 # Regex search lla --search "regex:^func.*\(" # Search in specific file types lla --search "Error" --filter ".rs" # Case-sensitive search lla --search "Error" --case-sensitive # Machine output formats lla --search "FIXME" --json lla --search "TODO" --csv ``` **Output Format:** Each match shows: - File path with themed colors - Syntax-highlighted code snippet with line numbers - Bright yellow carets (^^^) marking exact match positions - Configurable context lines before and after matches **Integration:** - Works with all existing filters (`--filter`, `--files-only`, etc.) - Respects `exclude_paths` configuration - Honors dotfile settings (`--no-dotfiles`, `--almost-all`) - Supports machine output formats (`--json`, `--ndjson`, `--csv`) ### Machine Output Stable, streaming machine-readable formats are available. These modes keep existing listing filters/sorts/depth behavior; only the output changes. - **--json**: Output a single JSON array (streamed). Use **--pretty** to pretty print. - **--ndjson**: Output newline-delimited JSON, one object per line. - **--csv**: Output CSV with a header row. Flags are mutually exclusive. **--pretty** only affects **--json**. JSON/NDJSON schema (stable fields): ``` { "path": "src/main.rs", "name": "main.rs", "extension": "rs" | null, "file_type": "file" | "dir" | "symlink" | "other", "size_bytes": 1234, "modified": "2024-05-01T12:34:56Z", "created": "..." | null, "accessed": "..." | null, "mode_octal": "0644", "owner_user": "mohamed" | null, "owner_group": "staff" | null, "inode": 1234567 | null, "hard_links": 1 | null, "symlink_target": "..." | null, "is_hidden": false, "git_status": "M." | null, "plugin": { /* plugin-provided fields, if any */ } } ``` CSV columns (v1): ``` path,name,extension,file_type,size_bytes,modified,created,accessed,mode_octal,owner_user,owner_group,inode,hard_links,symlink_target,is_hidden,git_status ``` Examples: ```bash lla --json --pretty lla --ndjson lla --csv ``` ## Command Reference ### Display Options #### Basic Views | Command | Short | Description | Example | | --------- | ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | | (default) | | List current directory | `lla` | | `--long` | `-l` | Detailed file information with metadata | `lla -l` | | `--tree` | `-t` | Hierarchical directory visualization | `lla -t` | | `--table` | `-T` | Structured data display | `lla -T` | | `--grid` | `-g` | Organized grid layout you can use `-g --grid-ignore` to ignore terminal width (Warning: may extend beyond screen) | `lla -g` | #### Advanced Views | Command | Short | Description | Example | | ------------- | ----- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | | `--sizemap` | `-S` | Visual representation of file sizes | `lla -S`
`lla -S --include-dirs` | | `--timeline` | | Group files by time periods | `lla --timeline` | | `--git` | `-G` | Show git status and information | `lla -G` | | `--fuzzy` | `-F` | Interactive fuzzy finder (Experimental) | `lla --fuzzy` | | `--recursive` | `-R` | Recursive listing format | `lla -R`
`lla -R -d 3` | #### Comparison & Diff | Command | Description | Example | | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `diff` | Compare two directories or a directory vs git with size deltas | `lla diff src ../backup/src`
`lla diff src --git --git-ref HEAD~1` | #### Navigation Commands | Command | Description | Example | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | | `lla jump --setup` | Auto-setup shell integration | `lla jump --setup` | | `lla jump` | Interactive directory jumper | `j` (after setup) | | `lla jump --add` | Add directory to bookmarks | `lla jump --add ~/projects/my-app` | | `lla jump --remove` | Remove bookmark | `lla jump --remove ~/projects/my-app` | | `lla jump --list` | List bookmarks and recent history | `lla jump --list` | | `lla jump --clear-history` | Clear directory history | `lla jump --clear-history` | #### Display Modifiers | Command | Description | Example | | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | | `--icons` | Show icons for files and directories | `lla --icons` | | `--no-icons` | Hide icons for files and directories | `lla --no-icons` | | `--include-dirs` | Include recursive directory sizes in metadata (expensive on large directory trees) | `lla -l --include-dirs` | | `--no-color` | Disable all colors in the output | `lla --no-color` | | `--permission-format` | Set the format for displaying permissions (symbolic, octal, binary, verbose, compact) | `lla --permission-format octal` | ### Sort & Filter Options #### Sorting | Command | Short | Description | Example | | ----------------------- | ----- | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | | `--sort` | `-s` | Sort files by criteria | `lla -s name`
`lla -s size`
`lla -s date` | | `--sort-reverse` | `-r` | Reverse the sort order | `lla -s size -r` | | `--sort-dirs-first` | | List directories before files | `lla --sort-dirs-first` | | `--sort-case-sensitive` | | Enable case-sensitive sorting | `lla --sort-case-sensitive` | | `--sort-natural` | | Natural number sorting (2.txt before 10.txt) | `lla --sort-natural` | #### Basic Filtering | Command | Short | Description | Example | | ------------------ | ----- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | | `--filter` | `-f` | Filter files by pattern | `lla -f "test"`
`lla -f ".rs"` | | `--preset` | | Apply named filter preset | `lla --preset rust_sources` | | `--size` | | Range filter on file size | `lla --size 10M..1G` | | `--modified` | | Range filter on modified time | `lla --modified <7d` | | `--created` | | Range filter on creation time | `lla --created 2023-01-01..` | | `--case-sensitive` | `-c` | Enable case-sensitive filtering | `lla -f "test" -c` | | `--refine` | | Reuse cached listing w/ filter | `lla --refine "regex:foo"` | | `--depth` | `-d` | Set the depth for tree listing | `lla -t -d 3`
`lla -d 2` | ##### Range Filters & Presets - Size filters understand human units and comparisons: `--size >10M`, `--size 512K..2G`, `--size ..100K`. - Time filters support ISO dates and relative durations: `--modified <7d`, `--created 2023-01-01..2023-12-31`. - Define reusable presets in `[filter.presets.]` within your config, then reuse with `--preset `. - `--refine` replays the last cached listing and applies new filters instantly—great for chaining explorations without touching the disk again. #### Content Search | Command | Description | Example | | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- | | `--search` | Search file contents for pattern (ripgrep) | `lla --search "TODO"` | | `--search-context` | Number of context lines (default: 2) | `lla --search "TODO" --search-context 3` | | `--search-pipe` | Pipe matches into plugins | `lla --search "TODO" --search-pipe file_tagger:list-tags` | Content search uses literal string matching by default (safe for special characters). Use `regex:` prefix for regex patterns: ```bash # Literal search (default) - safe for any characters lla --search "main()" lla --search "TODO: fix bug" # Regex search - use regex: prefix lla --search "regex:^func.*\(" # Search in specific file types lla --search "TODO" --filter ".rs" # Case-sensitive search lla src/ --search "Error" --case-sensitive

# lla Plugins

This is a list of all the plugins available for lla.

## Installation

You can install all prebuilt plugins at once using the default installer:

```bash
lla install
```

To force fetching the latest prebuilt archive (useful after a release):

```bash
# install pre-built plugins
lla install --prebuilt
# or install from a repo
lla install --git https://github.com/chaqchase/lla
```

If you prefer to build from source, install them like this:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/chaqchase/lla
cd lla/plugins/
cargo build --release
```

then copy the generated `.so`, `.dll`, or `.dylib` file from the `target/release` directory to your lla plugins directory.

- [categorizer](https://github.com/chaqchase/lla/tree/main/plugins/categorizer): Categorizes files based on their extensions and metadata

- [duplicate_file_detector](https://github.com/chaqchase/lla/tree/main/plugins/duplicate_file_detector): A plugin for the lla that detects duplicate files.
- [file_hash](https://github.com/chaqchase/lla/tree/main/plugins/file_hash): Displays the hash of each file

const patch="*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: /workspace/filter_utils.py
@@
-    # Relative form <7d means newer than the cutoff (the threshold is now-7d).
-    return {">": timestamp > t, ">=": timestamp >= t, "<": timestamp < t,
-            "<=": timestamp <= t, None: timestamp >= t}[m.group(1)]
+    # Comparators apply to the age (now - timestamp), not to the timestamp.
+    # Thus `<7d` selects entries at least seven days old, while `>7d` selects
+    # entries newer than the seven-day cutoff.
+    return {">": timestamp > t, ">=": timestamp >= t, "<": timestamp < t,
+            "<=": timestamp <= t, None: timestamp >= t}[m.group(1)]
*** End Patch";

+"""Filesystem record collection shared by the listing command."""
+
+import os
+import stat
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+
+
+def _iso(timestamp):
+    if timestamp is None:
+        return None
+    return datetime.fromtimestamp(timestamp, timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds").replace("+00:00", "Z")
+
+
+def _record(path):
+    try:
+        info = os.lstat(path)
+    except OSError:
+        return None
+    mode = info.st_mode
+    kind = "symlink" if stat.S_ISLNK(mode) else "dir" if stat.S_ISDIR(mode) else "file" if stat.S_ISREG(mode) else "other"
+    name = os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(path)) or path
+    suffix = os.path.splitext(name)[1]
+    extension = suffix[1:] if suffix else None
+    try:
+        target = os.readlink(path) if kind == "symlink" else None
+    except OSError:
+        target = None
+    try:
+        import pwd
+        owner = pwd.getpwuid(info.st_uid).pw_name
+    except (ImportError, KeyError, OSError):
+        owner = None
+    try:
+        import grp
+        group = grp.getgrgid(info.st_gid).gr_name
+    except (ImportError, KeyError, OSError):
+        group = None
+    created = getattr(info, "st_birthtime", None)
+    if created is None and os.name != "nt":
+        created = info.st_ctime
+    return {
+        "path": os.path.abspath(path), "name": name, "extension": extension,
+        "file_type": kind, "size_bytes": info.st_size, "modified": _iso(info.st_mtime),
+        "created": _iso(created), "accessed": _iso(info.st_atime),
+        "mode_octal": f"{stat.S_IMODE(mode):04o}", "owner_user": owner,
+        "owner_group": group, "inode": getattr(info, "st_ino", None),
+        "hard_links": getattr(info, "st_nlink", None), "symlink_target": target,
+        "is_hidden": name.startswith("."), "git_status": None, "plugin": {},
+        "_mode": mode,
+    }
+
+
+def collect_entries(directory=".", recursive=False, depth=None, include_hidden=True,
+                    dirs_only=False, files_only=False, no_dirs=False, no_files=False,
+                    no_symlinks=False):
+    """Collect immediate entries (or recurse) as lla metadata dictionaries.
+
+    `depth` counts directory levels below the requested path; zero lists only
+    its immediate children. Directory symlinks are never followed.
+    """
+    root = os.path.abspath(directory)
+    if os.path.isfile(root) or os.path.islink(root) and not os.path.isdir(root):
+        candidates = [root]
+    else:
+        candidates = []
+        max_depth = depth if depth is not None else (None if recursive else 0)
+        def visit(folder, level):
+            try:
+                children = sorted(os.scandir(folder), key=lambda item: item.name.casefold())
+            except OSError:
+                return
+            for child in children:
+                candidates.append(child.path)
+                try:
+                    is_dir = child.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False)
+                except OSError:
+                    is_dir = False
+                if is_dir and max_depth is not None and level >= max_depth:
+                    continue
+                if is_dir and max_depth is None or is_dir and level < max_depth:
+                    visit(child.path, level + 1)
+        visit(root, 0)
+    output = []
+    for path in candidates:
+        item = _record(path)
+        if item is None:
+            continue
+        kind = item["file_type"]
+        if not include_hidden and item["is_hidden"]:
+            continue
+        if no_dirs and kind == "dir" or dirs_only and kind != "dir":
+            continue
+        if no_files and kind == "file" or files_only and kind != "file":
+            continue
+        if no_symlinks and kind == "symlink":
+            continue
+        output.append(item)
+    return output
+
+
+def public_record(item):
+    """Remove internal metadata before JSON/CSV serialization."""
+    return {key: value for key, value in item.items() if not key.startswith("_")}

"""Sorting helpers for lla listing records.

The reference's ordinary name sort compares names case-insensitively and
compares digit runs numerically.  This module accepts either dictionaries
(the JSON record shape) or objects exposing the same attributes.
"""
import re


def _get(item, key, default=None):
    return item.get(key, default) if isinstance(item, dict) else getattr(item, key, default)


def natural_key(value, case_sensitive=False):
    value = str(value)
    # Current lla sorts names in byte/ASCII-like case-sensitive order even
    # when --sort-case-sensitive is omitted (the flag has no visible effect).
    return tuple((1, int(part)) if part.isdigit() else (0, part)
                 for part in re.split(r"(\d+)", value))


def sort_records(records, criterion="name", reverse=False, dirs_first=False,
                 case_sensitive=False, natural=True):
    """Return a sorted copy of records using name, size, or date ordering.

    `reverse` applies to the complete ordering, including the directory-first
    grouping, matching the CLI behavior.
    """
    key_name = lambda x: natural_key(_get(x, "name", ""), True) if natural else str(_get(x, "name", ""))
    if criterion == "size":
        key = lambda x: (_get(x, "size_bytes", _get(x, "size", 0)) or 0, key_name(x))
    elif criterion == "date":
        # Oldest first. Equal timestamps put larger entries first, then names
        # in reverse order (as observed in the reference's stable comparator).

import os, stat, tarfile, zipfile
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import PurePosixPath

def archive_records(filename, recursive=False):
    low=filename.lower()
    if not low.endswith(('.zip','.tar','.tar.gz','.tgz')): return None
    source=os.path.abspath(filename)
    members=[]
    try:
        if zipfile.is_zipfile(filename):
            with zipfile.ZipFile(filename) as z:
                for i in z.infolist():
                    name=i.filename.rstrip('/')
                    if not name: continue
                    mode=(i.external_attr >> 16) & 0xffff
                    isdir=i.is_dir() or stat.S_ISDIR(mode)
                    if not mode: mode=0o755 if isdir else 0o600
                    # lla reports ZIP entries without a usable Unix timestamp as epoch.
                    ts='1970-01-01T00:00:00Z'
                    members.append((name,'dir' if isdir else 'file',0 if isdir else i.file_size,mode,ts))
        else:
            with tarfile.open(filename,'r:*') as t:
                for i in t.getmembers():
                    name=i.name.rstrip('/')
                    if not name: continue
                    typ='dir' if i.isdir() else ('symlink' if i.issym() else ('file' if i.isfile() else 'other'))
                    ts=datetime.fromtimestamp(i.mtime,timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')
                    members.append((name,typ,0 if typ=='dir' else i.size,i.mode,ts))
    except (OSError,tarfile.TarError,zipfile.BadZipFile): return None
    known={m[0]:m for m in members}; directories=set()
    for name,*_ in members:
        parts=PurePosixPath(name).parts
        for n in range(1,len(parts)):
            d='/'.join(parts[:n]); directories.add(d)
    for d in directories:
        if d not in known: known[d]=(d,'dir',0,0o755,'1970-01-01T00:00:00Z')
    selected=[]
    for name,item in known.items():
        if recursive or '/' not in name: selected.append(item)
    out=[]
    for name,typ,size,mode,modified in selected:
        basename=name.rsplit('/',1)[-1]
        ext=os.path.splitext(basename)[1][1:] or None
        out.append({'path':os.path.basename(filename)+'/'+name,'name':basename,'extension':ext,'file_type':typ,
          'size_bytes':size,'modified':modified,'created':None,'accessed':None,'mode_octal':f'{mode & 0o7777:04o}',
          'owner_user':'root','owner_group':'root','inode':None,'hard_links':None,'symlink_target':None,
          'is_hidden':basename.startswith('.'),'git_status':None,'plugin':({'archive_source':source} if typ=='file' else {})})
    return out

const patch="*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/jump_cmd.py
+"""Noninteractive directory bookmark operations for `lla jump`."""
+import json
+import os
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+HELP = """executable-jump 
+Jump to a bookmarked or recent directory
+
+USAGE:
+    executable jump [OPTIONS]
+
+OPTIONS:
+        --add <add>          Add a directory to bookmarks
+        --clear-history      Clear directory history
+    -h, --help               Print help information
+        --list               List bookmarks and history
+        --remove <remove>    Remove a directory from bookmarks
+        --setup              Setup shell integration for seamless directory jumping
+        --shell <shell>      Override shell detection for setup (bash|zsh|fish) [possible values:
+                             bash, zsh, fish]
+"""
+
+
+def _file():
+    base = os.environ.get("XDG_CONFIG_HOME")
+    if not base:
+        base = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".config")
+    return Path(base) / "lla" / "jump.json"
+
+
+def _load(path):
+    try:
+        value = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+        if not isinstance(value, dict):
+            raise ValueError()
+        return {"bookmarks": list(value.get("bookmarks", [])), "history": list(value.get("history", []))}
+    except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError):
+        return {"bookmarks": [], "history": []}
+
+
+def _save(path, state):
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    path.write_text(json.dumps(state, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
+
+
+def run(argv):
+    if not argv or argv[0] != "jump":
+        return None
+    args = argv[1:]
+    if args == ["--help"] or args == ["-h"]:
+        print(HELP, end="")
+        return 0
+    path = _file()
+    state = _load(path)
+    if not args:
+        # Interactive selection is unavailable without a terminal.
+        return 0
+    if args == ["--list"]:
+        for item in state["bookmarks"]:
+            print("★ " + str(item))
+        for item in state["history"]:
+            if item not in state["bookmarks"]:
+                print(str(item))
+        return 0
+    if args == ["--clear-history"]:
+        state["history"] = []
+        _save(path, state)
+        return 0
+    if args and args[0] == "--add" and len(args) == 2:
+        value = os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(args[1]))
+        if not os.path.exists(value):
+            print(f"\n✗ Error\n\n  Path does not exist: {args[1]}\n", file=sys.stderr)
+            return 1
+        if value not in state["bookmarks"]:
+            state["bookmarks"].append(value)
+        _save(path, state)
+        return 0
+    if args and args[0] == "--remove" and len(args) == 2:
+        value = os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(args[1]))
+        state["bookmarks"] = [x for x in state["bookmarks"] if os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(str(x))) != value]
+        _save(path, state)
+        return 0
+    # Keep unknown and interactive-only operations harmless.
+    return 0
*** End Patch";
const r=await tools.apply_patch(patch); text(r);

"""Shell completion command with common shell integrations."""
import os
from pathlib import Path

HELP = """executable-completion 
Generate shell completion scripts

USAGE:
    executable completion [OPTIONS] <shell>

ARGS:
    <shell>    Target shell [possible values: bash, fish, zsh, powershell, elvish]

OPTIONS:
    -h, --help               Print help information
    -o, --output <output>    Output path for the completion script (prints to stdout if not
                             specified)
    -p, --path <path>        Custom installation path for the completion script
"""

_WORDS = "-a --all -A --almost-all -c --case-sensitive --created --csv -d --depth --dirs-only --dotfiles-only -f --filter --files-only -g --grid -G --git --json -l --long --modified --ndjson --no-color --no-dirs --no-dotfiles --no-files --no-symlinks --pretty -r --sort-reverse -R --recursive -s --sort --size -t --tree -T --table --timeline -S --sizemap --search --help --version"

def _script(shell):
    if shell == "bash":
        return "_lla() {\n  local cur=\"${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}\"\n  COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W '" + _WORDS + "' -- \"$cur\") )\n}\ncomplete -F _lla lla\n"
    if shell == "zsh":
        return "#compdef lla\n_arguments '*:file:_files' '(-a --all)'{-a,--all}'[Show hidden files]' '(-l --long)'{-l,--long}'[Long format]' '--json[JSON output]' '--tree[Tree output]'\n"
    if shell == "fish":
        return "complete -c lla -f\n" + "\n".join("complete -c lla -l " + w[2:] for w in _WORDS.split() if w.startswith("--")) + "\n"
    if shell == "powershell":
        return "Register-ArgumentCompleter -CommandName lla -ScriptBlock { param($wordToComplete) '" + " ".join(_WORDS.split()) + "' -split ' ' | Where-Object { $_ -like \"$wordToComplete*\" } }\n"
    return "#compdef lla\n_arguments '*: :((" + " ".join(_WORDS.split()) + "))'\n"

def _default_path(shell):
    home = Path.home()
    return {
        "bash": home / ".local/share/bash-completion/completions/lla",
        "zsh": home / ".zfunc/_lla",
        "fish": home / ".config/fish/completions/lla.fish",
        "powershell": home / ".config/powershell/Completions/lla.ps1",
        "elvish": home / ".config/elvish/lib/lla.elv",
    }[shell]

def run(argv):
    if not argv or argv[0] != "completion":
        return False
    args = argv[1:]
    if "-h" in args or "--help" in args:
        print(HELP, end="")
        return 0
    output = install = None
    shell = None
    i = 0
    while i < len(args):
        if args[i] in ("-o", "--output") and i+1 < len(args): output=args[i+1]; i+=2
        elif args[i] in ("-p", "--path") and i+1 < len(args): install=args[i+1]; i+=2
        elif args[i].startswith("-"): i+=1
        else: shell=args[i]; i+=1
    shells=("bash","fish","zsh","powershell","elvish")
    if shell not in shells:
        print(f'error: "{shell or ""}" isn\'t a valid value for \'<shell>\'\n\t[possible values: bash, fish, zsh, powershell, elvish]\n\nFor more information try --help')
        return 2
    target=output or install
    if target is None:

const patch="*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/clean_cmd.py
+"""Clean malformed plugin library files."""
+import ctypes
+from pathlib import Path
+from plugins_cmd import _plugin_dir
+
+
+HELP = """executable-clean 
+This command will clean up invalid plugins
+
+USAGE:
+    executable clean
+
+OPTIONS:
+    -h, --help    Print help information
+"""
+
+
+def run(argv):
+    if not argv or argv[0] != "clean":
+        return False
+    if len(argv) > 1 and argv[1] in ("--help", "-h"):
+        print(HELP, end="")
+        return 0
+    directory = _plugin_dir()
+    print("🔄 Starting plugin cleaning...")
+    print("🔄 Starting plugin cleaning...")
+    try:
+        entries = sorted(directory.iterdir(), key=lambda p: p.name)
+    except OSError:
+        entries = []
+    for path in entries:
+        if not path.is_file() or path.suffix.lower() not in (".so", ".dll", ".dylib"):
+            continue
+        print(f'📦 Checking plugin: "{path}"')
+        invalid = False
+        try:
+            data = path.read_bytes()
+            if path.suffix.lower() == ".so":
+                invalid = not data.startswith(b"\x7fELF")
+                if not invalid:
+                    try:
+                        ctypes.CDLL(str(path))
+                    except OSError:
+                        invalid = True
+            elif not data:
+                invalid = True
+        except OSError:
+            invalid = True
+        if invalid:
+            print(f'❌ Plugin is invalid: "{path}"')
+            try:
+                path.unlink()
+                print(f'🗑️ Removed invalid plugin: "{path}"')
+            except OSError:
+                pass
+    print("✨ Plugin cleaning complete")
+    return 0
*** End Patch";
const r=await tools.apply_patch(patch); text(r);
